operations.description:
Operator calls that named this account, newest first. Absent from the
binding journal by design: one call can move many accounts, and only
the call knows why it was made.

person_id.description: The binding in force now, if the account has one.

AccountMatchResponse.description: One account as a search answers for it: what it is, and whose it is.

bound_by_operator.description: `true` when a person decided this binding rather than automation.

excluded.description:
The account is deliberately excluded from person metrics (a bot, CI, a
service account). Without this an exclusion — an operator's recorded
decision — would read as "bound to nobody" and invite undoing it.

oneOf.description:
The person holding it, hydrated. Absent means nobody holds it yet —
except when `excluded` is set, which is a different fact entirely.

AccountOperationResponse.description:
One operator call that named this account.

The binding journal says what a decision did; this says who ran it, the
reason they gave, and how far it reached — a merge lands one row here and
one in every other account it moved.

accounts_touched.description: Accounts the call named, this one included.

oneOf.description: The author as a card, when the journal knows them by more than an id.

comment.description: What the operator typed, when they typed anything.

outcome.description:
What the call did to THIS account: `applied` | `already_decided` |
`refused`. A refusal changed nothing and still belongs in the trail.

AccountRef.description:
A source-native account, as named by the caller.

Addressing by an observed value (e-mail / username) instead of the account
triple is the reserved extension for importing a prepared matching table:
the fields arrive optional, exactly one form is required per item, a value
resolving to zero or several active accounts is reported per item and never
guessed. The response already carries per-item outcomes, so adding it does
not change the shape of this contract.

truncated.description: More accounts matched than `limit` allowed — narrow the terms.

items_truncated.description:
`limit` cut the item list — more accounts await a decision than are
listed here. Distinct from `truncated`: the rates stay whole-tenant,
only this page is short.

truncated.description:
The evidence read hit its safety cap: the queue and the rates describe
only the first accounts of the tenant, not all of them. Consumers must
not present these numbers as tenant-wide.

bindings.description: One or more bindings; a prepared matching table is submitted as one call.

new_person_id.description:
Set by `detach` when the account reached the new person; absent when
the write was refused, since no binding points at that id.

CreatePersonRoleRequest.description: Body of `POST /v1/person-roles` — grant a role to a person.

valid_from.description:
Optional assignment start; defaults to now when omitted. Accepts RFC-3339
(`Z`/offset), zone-less, or date-only, normalised to naive-UTC.

CreateVisibilityRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/visibility` — grant a viewer visibility over a target
(or the whole tree when `viewed_person_id` is omitted).

valid_from.description:
Optional grant start; defaults to now when omitted. Accepts RFC-3339
(`Z`/offset), zone-less, or date-only, normalised to naive-UTC.

HistoryEntry.description: One decision in an account's history.

oneOf.description: The operator who decided it; absent for automation, which has no card.

by_operator.description: `true` when a person made this decision, `false` for automation.

oneOf.description: The person this decision pointed at, as a card when one is known.

ItemResult.description: What happened to one requested account.

MeResponse.description: The caller as the gateway JWT identifies them, with their active roles.

MeRoleResponse.description: One active role assignment of the caller.

source_person_id.description: The person being absorbed — its accounts move to the target.

target_person_id.description: The surviving person, named explicitly by the operator.

bound_by_operator.description: `true` when the account's current binding was made by a person.

next_cursor.description: Wire parity with the other listings: declared, always `null`.

truncated.description:
More persons matched than `limit` allowed — the page is a cut, not the
answer, and the UI should ask for narrower terms. Without this flag a
truncated page reads as "the person does not exist".

PersonResponse.description:
A person node in the org tree (subordinate of a profile), matching the .NET
`PersonResponse`. Unlike `ProfileResponse`, the attribute fields are plain
strings (empty when absent, not omitted) and the `supervisor_*`/`parent_*`
fields serialize as `null` rather than being dropped.

next_cursor.description:
Wire parity with the .NET `ListResponse`: the cursor is declared
but pagination is not implemented — always `null` (both
implementations return every row; consumers already tolerate it).

PersonSummaryResponse.description:
A person as operator surfaces display them: enough to recognise and pick,
nothing more. Every field but the id may be null — a person the journal
knows only through bindings still appears, as the id alone.

provisional.description:
The journal holds nothing but a login-mint for this person: they exist
so somebody could sign in, and may duplicate one the roster knows. Not
a merge target — the history is on the other side.

username.description:
Source-native handle (e.g. a git login) — often the only recognisable
field of an identity no HR system has observed yet.

next_cursor.description:
Wire parity with the .NET `ListResponse`: the cursor is declared
but pagination is not implemented — always `null` (both
implementations return every row; consumers already tolerate it).

PersonsSeedOperationResponse.description:
One operation's status. Wire shape mirrors the .NET
`PersonsSeedOperationResponse`: `request` and `summary` are surfaced as
parsed JSON (not double-encoded strings), the tenant/author ids are
included, timestamps are ISO-8601, and null fields are emitted (the .NET
serializer does not drop nulls).

PersonsSyncListResponse.description:
List response wrapper (typed for OpenAPI). `next_cursor` is declared but
always `null` — same non-paginating contract as the seed journal.

PersonsSyncOperationResponse.description:
One operation's status. Wire shape matches the seed journal's:
`request` and `summary` surfaced as parsed JSON, ISO-8601 timestamps,
null fields emitted.

summary.description:
On completion: the [`SyncSummary`] — rows copied, `max_id` /
`max_created_at` watermarks, `synced_at`.

[`SyncSummary`]: crate::domain::sync_service::SyncSummary

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem+json. `context` varies by error category.

ProfileIdEntry.description:
One source-native account id bound to the person — the latest
`value_type='id'` observation per source instance. Ported from the .NET
`ProfileIdEntry`.

ProfileResponse.description:
Response body of `POST /v1/profiles` — the resolved person's profile:
current attributes, the org tree (`supervisor_*` / `parent_*` /
`subordinates[]`), and every current source-native id (`ids[]`). Null
attribute fields are omitted from JSON; `subordinates`/`ids` are always
present (empty when none), matching the .NET contract.

ids.description:
Every current source-native id for the person (one per source instance).
Always serialized — an empty array when the person has no ids — matching
the .NET contract (unlike the attributes above, which are omitted).

subordinates.description:
Recursive subordinates subtree (direct reports and their reports), on the
configured `org_chart` source. Always serialized (empty when none).

bound_to.description:
Who holds the account right now. Absent = nobody, which is what an
unbound account on the queue means; present, it names which of the
candidates below is the one being disagreed with.

candidates.description:
Persons this account could belong to, if any are known — hydrated into
cards so the operator UI never has to resolve bare ids itself.

display_name.description:
How the source describes the account. Nothing here is matchable — it is
what lets an operator recognise whose account this is when automation
cannot, which is exactly the case for the ones only they can bind.

ResolutionRatesResponse.description:
Share of observed accounts per resolution state — the operator-visible match
rate.

ResolveProfileRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/profiles`. `value_type = "email"` matches across all
sources for the tenant; `value_type = "id"` matches a source-native account
id within one source instance (needs `insight_source_type` + `insight_source_id`);
`value_type = "person_id"` takes the canonical person UUID itself — the key
the metrics runtime and its routes use since the identity cutover.

insight_source_type.description: Required when `value_type = "id"` — the source instance to scope to.

RevokeReasonRequest.description: Optional `DELETE` body carrying a revoke reason.

next_cursor.description:
Wire parity with the .NET `ListResponse`: the cursor is declared
but pagination is not implemented — always `null` (both
implementations return every row; consumers already tolerate it).

SubchartForestResponse.description:
`{ "roots": [ … ] }` — forest wrapper (#344). Empty when the caller has no
visible-in-source membership.

SubchartNode.description: One node in the org subchart tree.

SubchartResponse.description:
`{ "root": { … } }` — single-root wrapper (locked by the #348 acceptance
criteria so the response can gain sibling fields without breaking clients).

next_cursor.description:
Wire parity with the .NET `ListResponse`: the cursor is declared
but pagination is not implemented — always `null` (both
implementations return every row; consumers already tolerate it).

VisiblePersonsRequest.description:
Canonical person UUIDs to check (the metric runtime's key since the
identity cutover — the earlier email-based draft of this endpoint never
shipped).

info.description: Person identity for the product: profile resolution, the operator correction surface over account-to-person bindings, org-chart reads, roles and visibility, plus the persons-seed and persons-sync operation journals. The API Gateway mounts this service at /api/identity.
